rounds.text: Kalyan Jewellers is exhibiting elite fundamental momentum that fundamentally outpaces its past share price growth, leaving a massive window of opportunity for re-pricing [E52]. Over the last five years, profit has compounded at an astonishing 195% while share price growth lagged at 54% [E17, E20]. This divergence is further underscored by recent data showing profit growth outpacing one-year price growth by 42% [E53]. The business is generating substantial internal resources, posting an operating cash flow of Rs 1,318 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 939 Cr as of March 2026 [E31, E32]. Institutional confidence is firmly behind this operational excellence, demonstrated by domestic institutions increasing their stake by 8.93 percentage points and a positive institutional money flow rating of +1.59 percentage points [E39, E40]. Furthermore, management has successfully achieved a milestone by becoming completely debt-free on non-GML borrowings while simultaneously scaling store expansions [E72, E82]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 41.9x and a P/B of 9.94x [E1, E2].

The current valuation of Kalyan Jewellers is severely stretched and offers virtually no margin of safety to investors, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at ₹632 per share, which sits below the prevailing market price of ₹639 and leaves a negative margin of safety of -1.1% [E41, E42]. Furthermore, the stock trades at an expensive price-to-earnings ratio of 41.9x and a price-to-book multiple of 9.94x, heavily outstripping the broader sector benchmark price-to-book ratio of 2x [E1, E2, E7]. This high valuation requires perfection, with a reverse DCF indicating that the market price already bakes in an aggressive 18.1% future earnings growth rate [E43]. Significant institutional capital is also retreating from the name, demonstrated by foreign institutional investors slashing their stake from 26.21% in December 2023 down to 13.83% by September 2026 [E38]. Additionally, the underlying business is burdened by persistent total borrowings of ₹6,127 Cr as of September 2026, which have actually crept upward compared to the ₹6,117 Cr recorded a year prior [E35]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong compounding sales growth of 33% over 5 years alongside a healthy return on equity of 24.8% [E14, E13].

Conceded: intrinsic value sits at ₹632 per share against a market price of ₹639, leaving a negative margin of safety of -1.1% [E41, E42]. However, dismissing the stock on valuation ignores superior operational quality, where return on equity of 24.8% and return on capital employed of 21.2% completely dwarf sector benchmarks of 8.89% and 10.28% [E7, E9, E10, E13]. While the bear highlights foreign institutional reduction, this capital has been more than absorbed by domestic institutions increasing their stake by 8.93 percentage points alongside a positive overall institutional money flow [E38, E39, E40]. The concern over total borrowings is also misplaced because the company successfully completed its non-GML debt repayment by the end of September as planned, transforming that part of the balance sheet and unlocking collateral [E71, E82]. Furthermore, the required 18.1% earnings growth implied by the reverse DCF is well supported by management's baseline projection of a minimum 25% revenue growth alongside aggressive showroom expansion targets for Kalyan and Candere [E43, E70, E72]. Finally, the robust fundamental momentum is underscored by a rules-based screen score of 93 out of 100 alongside trailing twelve-month profit growth of 69% [E19, E59].

The bull relies on high returns on equity and capital to justify the current price, yet these metrics must be weighed against a price-to-book ratio of 10.28x, which is more than five times the sector benchmark of 2x [E7, E9, E13]. While the bull points to domestic institutional buying, it ignores the significant exit of foreign institutions, whose holdings dropped from 26.21% to 13.83%—a massive reduction of 12.38 percentage points [E38, E39]. Conceded: the company has made progress on non-GML debt, yet total borrowings remain elevated at Rs 6,127 Cr, showing an increase over the prior year despite these efforts [E35, E71, E82]. The bull claims the 18.1% implied growth is supported by management, but this ignores that operating margins have remained stagnant at 7% over the last three years, suggesting that scaling revenue does not necessarily translate into improved operational efficiency [E26, E43]. Furthermore, the reliance on a 93/100 screen score ignores the "valuation blind-spot" warning that the current price already discounts the majority of the company's positive news [E59, E64]. Finally, the stock’s historical volatility, evidenced by a peak-to-trough drawdown of -57.9%, highlights the substantial risk inherent in chasing a stock that is already trading at a negative margin of safety [E42, E49].

The bear’s focus on the price-to-book ratio [E7] ignores that Kalyan’s superior capital efficiency, evidenced by an ROE of 24.8% [E13] and ROCE of 21.2% [E12], fundamentally justifies a premium valuation compared to a sector median ROCE of only 10.3% [E69]. While the bear highlights the reduction in foreign institutional holdings [E38], it fails to acknowledge the significant 8.93 percentage point increase in domestic institutional ownership [E39] and the overall positive money flow [E40], indicating a shift toward more stable, long-term local confidence. Conceded: total borrowings remain at Rs 6,127 Cr [E35], yet the company has successfully become debt-free on non-GML obligations [E82], demonstrating a clear and effective path toward balance sheet deleveraging. The claim of stagnant margins [E26] overlooks the reality that the company is aggressively scaling through store expansion [E72] and achieving massive compounded profit growth of 195% over five years [E17], proving that revenue growth is indeed translating into significant bottom-line expansion. Furthermore, the "valuation blind-spot" [E64] is countered by the fact that the company is consistently outperforming sector benchmarks for sales [E68] and profit growth [E67], with management explicitly guiding for a minimum of 25% revenue growth [E70]. Finally, the historical drawdown [E49] is a feature of a high-growth stock, but the current Sharpe ratio of 1.07 [E51] and the fact that the stock is trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E46] suggest that the current momentum is supported by strong fundamental performance rather than mere speculation.

Conceded: ROE is 24.8% [E13] and ROCE is 21.2% [E12]. However, paying a price-to-book ratio of 9.94x [E2]—which towers over the sector benchmark of 2x [E7]—prices in perfection while ignoring that operating margins are completely flat at 7% over a three-year period with an inconsistent trend [E26, E28]. While domestic institutions increased holdings [E39], foreign institutional investors drastically dumped 12.38 percentage points of their stake [E38], signalling severe caution from global capital. Conceded: non-GML debt has been cleared [E82]; nevertheless, total borrowings remain substantial at Rs 6,127 Cr [E35], and the current ratio sits at a thin buffer of 1.30x [E34]. The discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 632 against a higher market price of Rs 639, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -1.1% [E41, E42]. Finally, the reverse DCF confirms that today's price already demands an aggressive 18.1% earnings growth rate [E43], and the stock carries a harrowing historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -57.9% [E49] coupled with high annualized volatility of 45.9% [E50].
